subject.title: State schema migration bumps the on-disk version in place with no pre-migration backup, so a forward upgrade cannot be rolled back

question: Should OpenClaw guarantee an automatic pre-migration state-database snapshot for forward schema upgrades, and should inability to create that snapshot warn or block the migration?
rationale: This choice defines a persistent operator recovery promise and its availability tradeoff; the linked PR intentionally leaves best-effort versus fail-closed behavior open.

options.title: Adopt a bounded best-effort backup
options.body: Create a versioned pre-migration snapshot, surface failures prominently, and document how operators restore it without blocking otherwise healthy startup.

options.title: Require the backup before migration
options.body: Abort a forward migration when the recovery snapshot cannot be created, prioritizing rollback safety over startup availability.

options.title: Keep manual backups only
options.body: Retain the current migration behavior and direct operators to create backups before upgrades, avoiding a new automatic storage artifact.

recommendation.title: Adopt a bounded best-effort backup
recommendation.body: Create a versioned pre-migration snapshot, surface failures prominently, and document how operators restore it without blocking otherwise healthy startup.
